edges.description: Thr58Ile and Gly12Val NRAS increase basal AKT signaling in transfected cells, in parallel with ERK. The complete PI3K-mediated route is not directly dissected in this experiment.
Excess signaling is implicated in the NrasG12D mouse cardiac defects, with ERK, BMP and Wnt changes; their individual causal contributions remain unresolved.
Constitutive dysregulation of RAS-MAPK signalling underlies the reduced growth of the disorder.
The characteristic craniofacial appearance emerges from RAS-MAPK dysregulation during development, as it does across the RASopathies.
Activated N-Ras signalling perturbs early embryonic morphogenetic movements; MEK inhibition fully reverses the effect, establishing that the defect is MAPK-mediated.
Provisional extrapolation from RASopathy HCM models and pathway-directed rescue; human NRAS HCM is established clinically, but an NRAS-specific myocardial cellular route has not been demonstrated.
Constitutional RAS-MAPK dysregulation is implicated in Noonan cognitive deficits; the precise neuronal circuit and contribution of non-neural factors remain unresolved in NRAS cases.
Qualified pathway-level explanation shared with Noonan syndrome. In the CFCS-like NRAS case, perinatal injury and hydrocephalus may additionally influence cognitive outcome.
Provisional extrapolation from other RAS/MAPK-associated Noonan models in which ERK-driven SOX18 overexpression produces excessive lymphatic endothelial proliferation.

Provisional application of the broader RASopathy mechanism: disrupted Ras signaling alters septal formation. This is not inferred from the NrasG12D mouse ventricular defect, and the NRAS-specific atrial lineage mechanism remains unresolved.

nodes.description: Developmentally abnormal lymphatic channels and transport can impair lymph clearance, causing stasis, reflux and fluid accumulation. nodes.description: Heterozygous germline NRAS variants increase signaling through allele-dependent mechanisms. Gly60Glu resists GAP stimulation and accumulates in the GTP-bound state; Thr50Ile enhances signaling without increased GTP loading, with altered membrane orientation proposed. Ile24Asn may alter nucleotide affinity, whereas Thr58Ile and oncogenic Gly12 variants can increase basal signaling. Thus increased nucleotide exchange and stimulus dependence are not universal. Constitutional origin should be assessed in non-hematopoietic tissue because NRAS is also a somatic oncogene.

The authors propose allele-dependent risk, but small, age-heterogeneous series do not establish absolute risk or absence of risk for non-hotspot alleles.
